title: SQL
body:
The query language of relational databases, and by extension the usual shorthand for that whole family — Postgres, [[MySQL]], SQLite, SQL Server. Data lives in **tables** (a shelf holding one type of item), each row is one record, each column is one attribute every record has, and a [[Primary Key]] uniquely identifies a row.

What makes it *relational* is the [[Foreign Key]]: a column on one table pointing at another table's primary key, letting a [[JOIN]] recombine them in a single query. The defining property versus [[NoSQL]] is the enforced **schema** — every row in a table has the same shape, and the database itself rejects anything that violates that, along with constraints and transactional guarantees. Queries execute on the database server, which is usually a separate machine from the app server; the app just sends the query and receives the result. Fast lookups come from a [[Database Index]].
